clue.text: Bath perhaps welcoming female climber

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Bath is the classic English spa town, so it is an example of a spa
the feminine pronoun

explanation.surface: A woman mountaineer is being hosted in the city of Bath.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is a Somerset city famous for its Roman spring waters; the 'perhaps' marks it as one example of a spa.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are Himalayan people famed as mountain guides and porters, so one is a climber.

clue.text: Support commanding officer in post

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other, sitting within its letters

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
CO is the standard military abbreviation

explanation.surface: Backing up the commander who has been placed in a new posting.
explanation.definitionFit: To second a motion or proposal is to back it formally, a verb synonym of support.

clue.text: Formation of the ruling class

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the act of founding or setting something up
second meaning: the powerful elite who control society

explanation.surface: How the elite came to be formed.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both the founding of an institution and, with 'the', the dominant group holding power in a country.

clue.text: Operation sees old Conservative obstructing newspapers

indicators.note: something obstructing a passage sits in the middle of it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: the press is the newspapers collectively
O is a standard abbreviation for old
C abbreviates Conservative

explanation.surface: A surgical procedure sees a veteran Tory standing in the way of journalists.
explanation.definitionFit: A process is a series of actions or a procedure, so it is a synonym of an operation in the working sense.

clue.text: Some sponsor a clerical authority

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are wanted, a run taken from inside the words

parts.note: the run starts near the end of the first word and ends partway through the third

explanation.surface: Some backer of the church is an authority on clerical matters.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle is someone regarded as an infallible source of wisdom, so an authority or expert.

clue.text: Dance and drink with returning sailor

parts.note: rum is a spirit, the sailor's traditional drink

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A night of dancing and drinking alongside a sailor home from sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance in quick rhythm, so the answer is one example.

clue.text: Are conditions at sea a factor?

indicators.note: to be at sea is to be confused and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written: thirteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A sailor wondering whether the weather on the ocean matters.
explanation.definitionFit: A consideration is something to be taken into account when deciding, which is a factor in the decision.

clue.text: Job Elizabeth I managed diligently at first

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of a Queen Elizabeth
to run a business is to manage it

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter only of the word it follows

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: The Tudor queen applied herself to a task diligently from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Latin for Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a short trip to do a small task for someone, so it is a minor job.

clue.text: Dish fit for a queen?

parts.note: surface reading: a meal grand enough to serve royalty
setter's reading: a queen is also a female cat, so this is a dish for a pet

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'fit for a queen' suggests a banquet, but a queen here is a she-cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A female cat is called a queen, and the meal put in its bowl is pet food for felines.

clue.text: Rebellious Democrat insisted on reform

parts.note: D abbreviates Democrat

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A defiant Democratic politician demanded political change.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissident opposes official policy, so as an adjective it means defiant toward authority.

clue.text: Report of behaviour in country house

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word wanted sounds like the one given

parts.note: manner means way of behaving, and sounds the same as the answer

explanation.surface: An account of how people conduct themselves at a stately home.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor is the main house of a landed estate in the countryside.

clue.text: Distinguished prize-giver moving east

indicators.note: east is the right-hand way on a map, so a letter shifts rightwards to rearrange the word

parts.note: Alfred Nobel founded the Nobel Prizes

explanation.surface: An eminent awards founder relocating to the east.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly the E (east) moves one place to the right, east on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble describes someone of high rank or fine character, an adjective synonym of distinguished.

clue.text: Post for Paddington?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a place where someone is assigned to stand or serve
second meaning: Paddington is a London railway terminus, an example of a stop for trains

explanation.walkthrough: Paddington suggests the bear from the children's books, sent by post with a label; it is also a mainline London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry's assigned spot is called a station, and Paddington is an example of a railway one.

clue.text: Set up an academy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to establish or start something
second meaning: a society or organisation devoted to learning

explanation.surface: Founding a school of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to establish or begin, and as a noun it names an educational or learned organisation.

clue.text: Ignorant of tune lacking intro about a conflict

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened word goes round the rest
lacking its introduction means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a tune is a melody; it loses its first letter
taken as written
a war is an armed conflict

explanation.surface: Someone who has never heard an anthem whose opening concerns a war.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unaware of something means having no knowledge of it, the same as being ignorant of it.

clue.text: Friend turning up with excellent computer

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means read from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a pal is a friend
top means first-rate, excellent

explanation.surface: A mate arrives carrying a first-class computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A laptop is a portable personal computer small enough to rest on your knees.

clue.text: Patch up two Royal Engineers?

parts.note: RE abbreviates the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a pair is two of something

explanation.surface: A couple of army engineers are called in to mend something.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'two' as a number of engineers; cryptically the abbreviation comes first, then a word for two. The Royal Engineers are the British Army's corps of military engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair something is to mend or fix it, which is to patch it up.

clue.text: Two articles about grant for long jumper?

parts.note: the first article: the indefinite one

indicators.note: about means around, so the second article goes round the next word

parts.note: the second article: the definite one
to let is to allow or grant

explanation.surface: Two newspaper pieces discussing funding awarded to a jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long jumper' is a specific track and field event competitor, given with a question mark as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A long jumper is a track and field competitor, so is an example of a sportsperson in athletics.

clue.text: First Lady inspiring Bill's escape

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so the first woman takes the next piece inside

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis
a bill is a poster, an advertisement, abbreviated AD

explanation.surface: The President's wife spurs Bill on to break out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' looks like a President's wife, especially beside Bill; it is Eve from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to escape or avoid something, used here as a noun-like synonym in the sense of getting away.

clue.text: American Indian leaving hospital very quickly

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so that letter goes out of the word

parts.note: the Apache are a Native American people
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A Native American rushes out of hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace is an adverb meaning swiftly, at a fast pace.

clue.text: Letter Goethe tantalisingly conceals

indicators.note: what is concealed sits inside, so the letters lie within the words around it

parts.note: the run spans the end of the poet's name and the start of the adverb

explanation.surface: The German poet writes a teasing letter that hides something.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Terrible strain, meeting a Russian ruler

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad way, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written: the letters to rearrange
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dreadful tension when meeting the ruler of Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' recalls Ivan the Terrible, a tsar, and leans the reader toward a male ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was an empress of Russia or the wife of a tsar, so a Russian sovereign.

clue.text: Old man in Rome with extra time for sales pitch

indicators.note: having something extra means an addition is slipped in among the letters

parts.note: pater is Latin for father, and 'old man' is slang for one's father
T abbreviates time

explanation.surface: An elderly Roman spending more time on a sales speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old man in Rome' is a Latin clue: the language of Rome's word for father.
explanation.definitionFit: Patter is the rapid, glib talk of a salesperson or entertainer, so a sales pitch.

clue.text: Singer said to be getting this in payment?

indicators.note: said points to how a word sounds when spoken, not its spelling

parts.note: a tenor is a high male singing voice

explanation.surface: A vocalist is reportedly being paid this.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A ten-pound note is a sum of money handed over, so this is the form the payment takes.
